name: Nonnus of Panopolis
bio: Nonnus of Panopolis, a town in Upper Egypt (modern Akhmim), was a Greek epic poet who flourished in the 5th century AD. Little is known of his life; he is thought to have been a pagan, or perhaps a convert to Christianity, writing in the Greek-speaking culture of late antique Egypt.

His major surviving work is the Dionysiaca, a hexameter epic in forty-eight books, at more than twenty thousand lines the longest poem to survive from antiquity. It tells of the birth, wanderings and Indian campaign of the god Dionysus and his eventual triumph, in a lavish, mannered style that deeply influenced later Greek poetry. He is also credited with a verse Paraphrase of the Gospel of John.
